memory_candidates.content: When building a script that must establish a yes/no admissibility verdict already computed by an existing, trusted predicate script, never re-derive the predicate -- shell out to the real script and read its structured output (NDJSON/JSON verdict objects with a discriminator field like defer_reason), bounding the number of invocations with a named cap constant if the caller searches over multiple candidate sets. A second copy of a collision/overlap predicate will drift from the real one, and a suggestion the real predicate later refuses is worse than no suggestion.

In this codebase's shared deploy-root-guard.sh pattern, a script that computes PROJECT_ROOT via common_repo_root(SCRIPT_DIR, 2) BEFORE sourcing deploy-root-guard.sh gets NO benefit from DEPLOY_ROOT_GUARD_SELF_CORRECT=1 when invoked from the source store: self-correct only sets $REPO_ROOT, which the caller must explicitly re-read AFTER sourcing the guard to actually use it. A script following the 'orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh' convention (PROJECT_ROOT computed first, guard sourced after, never opting into self-correct) cannot be live-tested from the source store at all -- test it via a temporary, gitignored copy under .claude/scripts/ instead (remove after testing, never commit).

update-task-status.sh's map_status() has a CLOSED operation:target_status vocabulary with no combination that resolves to state.json status 'not_started' -- every other status (researching/researched/planning/planned/implementing/partial/blocked/pr_ready/hold) has a resolving no-op token, but a task still in its initial status cannot receive a --depends-on-add (or any other) no-op status call via this script today. Any future caller of --depends-on-add must handle this case explicitly (loud fallback, never a silent drop or a guessed/wrong command) rather than assuming every live status is addressable.
